purpose: AUTOHAWK flipper-oriented model knowledge. Conservative starter database, not a mechanical guarantee.

good_gearboxes: DSG DQ250 wet with service proof
typical_problems: Golf 5/6 rear arches and sills can rust
TSI chain rattle on cold start
cards.flip_notes: Golf 5/6 has huge demand and can be the most profitable of the cheap candidates if bought very low. A Golf 5 around 1200 EUR can be a real HOT lead, but only if engine, TUV and rust are acceptable.
cards.avoid_notes: Most comfortable/pleasant candidate, but also higher repair risk than Yaris/Corsa/Fabia. Rust on arches/sills, gearbox issues, warning lights or weak TSI/DSG proof must cut the score hard.

typical_problems: small petrol engines can be reliable but need service
timing chain noise on some TSI
cards.flip_notes: Very liquid first-car model. Cosmetic issues can be good buying angle.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid sporty/TSI/DSG without proof; small cheap Polo must still have TUV.

cards.flip_notes: Kombi diesel is liquid for families/work. High mileage accepted if history is strong.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap diesel automatic with no service proof is dangerous.

cards.flip_notes: 7-seat/family demand is strong. Rough interior can be cheap prep if mechanics are clean.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid neglected family car with no TUV or TSI/DSG risk.

cards.flip_notes: SUV demand helps resale, but repair reserve must be bigger.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap Tiguan diesel/DSG can eat margin quickly.

cards.flip_notes: Very useful vehicle, sells to trades/families. High mileage okay with proof.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid abused work van with hidden rust or no service.

cards.flip_notes: One of the best flipper models if diesel/manual/history is honest. Kombi demand huge.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not buy ex-taxi/fleet without proof; watch mileage wear.

cards.flip_notes: Practical, cheap to own and simple. Good backup candidate, but older Fabia is less emotional/comfortable than Corsa/Yaris, so it needs either very clean condition or a clear price edge.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not call it a strong deal at normal market price. Old Fabia with weak TUV, rust or neglected 1.2 HTP is only average.

cards.flip_notes: Huge space; good diesel kombi can sell well, but buyer pool is smaller than Octavia.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid petrol TSI/DSG with no proof and very high mileage.

cards.flip_notes: Young buyers like it; FR/clean spec can sell fast.
cards.avoid_notes: Sporty abused TSI/DSG can become expensive.

cards.flip_notes: Liquid cheap car if simple engine/manual and TUV.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid cheap sporty TSI/DSG with no history.

typical_problems: Astra H/J rust and suspension wear
M32 gearbox bearings on some manuals
cards.flip_notes: Strong enough demand, especially caravan/sports tourer. Good TUV/service matters.
cards.avoid_notes: High mileage diesel without DPF/EGR/timing proof is weak flip.

typical_problems: timing chain rattle on small petrol if neglected
cards.flip_notes: Best cheap price/quality candidate when simple petrol/manual and TUV is okay. Around 1000 EUR can be very interesting because repairs are cheap and buyer pool is broad.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not overrate a Corsa only because it is cheap. No TUV, chain noise, Easytronic, heavy rust or cooling issues can erase the margin.
must_check: timing chain noise on cold start

cards.flip_notes: 7-seat demand exists but condition matters. Good TUV can sell.
cards.avoid_notes: Old diesel 7-seater with no proof is usually not a sweet deal.

cards.flip_notes: Can look cheap because demand is weaker. Only buy with big margin.
cards.avoid_notes: Not as liquid as Astra; do not overpay.

cards.flip_notes: Liquid compact if manual/simple engine. Good cheap Focus sells.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid PowerShift and neglected EcoBoost unless huge discount.

cards.flip_notes: Good first-car liquidity. Manual petrol with TUV is easy.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not buy cheap EcoBoost without belt proof.

cards.flip_notes: Kombi can sell, but not fast. Needs strong discount.
cards.avoid_notes: Weak liquidity compared with Passat/Octavia.

cards.flip_notes: 7-seat/family appeal, but repair risk must be priced in.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap automatic diesel can be a trap.

typical_problems: rust underside/rear axle on older cars
cards.flip_notes: Top safety/liquidity pick among cheap cars. XP90/Yaris is not always huge-margin, but it is easy to resell, trusted, cheap to maintain and often loses little money if bought correctly.
cards.avoid_notes: Still reject if no TUV plus serious rust, MMT gearbox issue, accident suspicion or seller cannot prove basic history.
must_check: manual gearbox/clutch or MMT warning signs

cards.flip_notes: Boring but very sellable. Trust is high.
cards.avoid_notes: Diesel/rough import/accident car less desirable.

cards.flip_notes: Good first-car/family trust. Hybrid sells well if clean.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid high-price non-hybrid with weak spec.

bad_gearboxes: old automatic issues rare but check
cards.flip_notes: Reliable image but slower resale than Corolla/Yaris. Good if cheap and clean.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid 2.2 diesel/D-CAT unless very strong proof.

cards.flip_notes: Very trusted small car. High mileage okay if rust/TUV/service good.
cards.avoid_notes: No TUV + rusty Jazz is not a bargain.

cards.flip_notes: Good reputation; clean petrol manuals sell well.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid modified/abused cars and i-Shift complaints.

cards.flip_notes: Solid budget car, good if TUV long and price right.
cards.avoid_notes: Not as emotional; overpriced cars sit.

cards.flip_notes: Good value compact; clean cars sell to practical buyers.
cards.avoid_notes: Weak spec/high price slows resale.

cards.flip_notes: Budget first-car demand. Warranty history helps trust.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid no-TUV tired cheap car.

cards.flip_notes: Good practical compact, less fear than old German risky motors.
cards.avoid_notes: Needs price advantage; brand is trusted but not premium.

typical_problems: rust is main enemy on older Mazdas
cards.flip_notes: Mechanically good, but rust decides. Clean body can be nice.
cards.avoid_notes: Rusty Mazda is not a bargain.

cards.flip_notes: Petrol manual with clean body is good. Diesel needs caution.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid rust and Skyactiv-D with emissions issues.

cards.flip_notes: Can be good if petrol and clean, but resale slower.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap diesel Mazda 6 is often a risk trap.

cards.flip_notes: SUV demand helps. Manual petrol/diesel with proof sells.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid CVT unless very strong proof and price.

cards.flip_notes: Cheap first car, okay if simple and TUV.
cards.avoid_notes: Weak German resale compared with Polo/Yaris, need price edge.

cards.flip_notes: Very cheap city car; profit only if bought very cheap with TUV.
cards.avoid_notes: Small margins; no TUV usually not worth it.

cards.flip_notes: Needs strong discount because demand weaker.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not buy around market price.

cards.flip_notes: Cheap and simple. Buyers like low running costs.
cards.avoid_notes: Margins small; condition/TUV must be good.

cards.flip_notes: SUV shape sells. Simple spec okay.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid abused 4x4 and rusty underside.

good_engines: later PureTech only with belt proof
cards.flip_notes: Looks modern and sells, but PureTech proof is everything.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap PureTech without belt/invoice is not a deal.

cards.flip_notes: Needs large discount; less liquid than Golf/Astra/Focus.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not buy around market with PureTech/THP risk.

cards.flip_notes: Can work only if very cheap with TUV.
cards.avoid_notes: Weak liquidity; do not chase normal-price cars.

cards.flip_notes: Style sells, especially clean cheap petrol manual.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid Dualogic unless very cheap and proven.

cards.flip_notes: Strong badge demand. Only good with clean history and right engine.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap TFSI/S-tronic can erase margin.

cards.flip_notes: Badge sells but risk is high. Need strong discount and proof.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid Multitronic and cheap big diesel unless exceptional.

bad_gearboxes: automatic no proof on high mileage
cards.flip_notes: Young buyers like it; clean spec sells. Risk must be priced in.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap N47/N43 without proof is dangerous.

cards.flip_notes: Huge demand but buyers know risks. Proof sells.
cards.avoid_notes: Do not buy just because cheap BMW.

cards.flip_notes: Badge helps; compact Mercedes sells if clean.
cards.avoid_notes: Avoid old CVT/Autotronic with any symptom.

cards.flip_notes: Practical family Mercedes; not super fast but steady.
cards.avoid_notes: CVT issues kill profit.

cards.flip_notes: Good badge demand. Clean estate/sedan can sell, but repairs are not cheap.
cards.avoid_notes: Cheap C-Class with no proof is not automatically good.

cards.flip_notes: Very liquid van/bus market. High mileage accepted if clean and documented.
cards.avoid_notes: Repair costs are huge; only buy with strong discount/proof.

bad_gearboxes: ASG automated manual if jerky/no proof
cards.flip_notes: VW Up is very liquid as a cheap city/first car, but dealer/Automarkt listings usually already include retail margin. Good for normal buyer, weak for flipper unless clearly below private-market price.
cards.avoid_notes: If from Autohaus/Automarkt and only around market price, cap score hard. For flipping, require clear discount, clean TUV and no accident/rust/warning-light issue.
